'''Hokushin Myōken Shrine''' (北辰妙見神社, ''Hokushin Myōken Jinja'') is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in [[Katsuragi]], [[:en:Ito District|Ito District]], [[Wakayama Prefecture]], Japan. The shrine enshrines [[Myōken|Myōken-son]] as its principal deity. It is notable for its historic bell, which has been designated as a [[tangible cultural property]].

== History and Overview ==
The shrine's exact founding date is unknown, but it is mentioned in the ''[[Kii Zoku Fudoki]]'' under the name "Myōken-sha" in the section on Takimura in [[Shigo Village]]. The shrine is associated with [[:en:Pole Star|Polaris]] and the [[Big Dipper]], collectively referred to as ''Hokushin'' ("Northern Stars") and regarded as the central axis of heaven. These stars were deified as ''Myōken-son'' and are commonly referred to as "Myōken-sama." Myōken-son is a foundational deity in [[Onmyōdō]] and [[Feng shui]].

The original shrine building was constructed in the ''Gongen-zukuri'' architectural style but was rebuilt in the [[Meiji era]] in the ''Nagare-zukuri'' style with vibrant coloration. Regular renovations occur every 20 years, with the most recent in 1994, during which the shrine's colors were restored and the worship hall rebuilt.

The Taki district has long been a hub of fervent religious devotion. Nearby are five temples and sacred halls. In addition to the shrine's own cultural assets, the area features significant artifacts, such as the [[:en:National Treasure|National Treasure]] bronze "Half-Seated Maitreya Bodhisattva" statue (from the [[Hakuhō period]]) at Gokuraku-ji Temple and a prefectural cultural property, the ''Daihannya Kyō'' (Great Wisdom Sutra), consisting of 569 scrolls dating back to [[1227]] (''Karoku'' 3).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.katsuragi-kanko.jp/search/syazi/%e5%8c%97%e8%be%b0%e5%a6%99%e8%a6%8b%e7%a5%9e%e7%a4%be/|title=北辰妙見神社|publisher=Katsuragi Town Tourism Association|accessdate=2020-11-03}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=4017|title=北辰妙見神社|publisher=Wakayama Shrine Office|accessdate=2020-11-03}}</ref>

== Enshrined Deities ==
* '''Principal deity:''' [[Myōken|Myōken-son]]
* '''Sub-Deities:'''
** [[Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Susanoo]]
** [[Emperor Ōjin|Hondawake-no-Mikoto]] (linked to [[Emperor Ōjin]])
** [[Miketsu no Mikoto]] (one of the [[Sumiyoshi sanjin|Sumiyoshi Sanjin]])
** [[Ichikishima-hime no Mikoto]] (a goddess of the sea and one of the [[Munakata Sanjin]])

== Cultural Assets and Grounds ==
=== Bell Tower ===
* The shrine's bronze bell dates to ''Bunei'' 2 (1265) and was designated a [[Wakayama Prefecture]] tangible cultural property on April 14, 1965.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.town.katsuragi.wakayama.jp/020/070/20170406185058.html|title=指定文化財一覧（県指定文化財）|publisher=Katsuragi Town|accessdate=2020-11-03}}</ref>

=== Shrine Buildings ===
The grounds include:
* '''Main Hall''' (''Nagare-zukuri'' style with copper roofing)
* '''Ebisu Shrine''' (''Nagare-zukuri'' style)
* '''Worship Hall''' (wooden, tiled roof)
* '''Star Service Hall''' (''Hoshi Kuyo-do'', wooden, tiled roof)
* '''Shrine Office''' (wooden, tiled roof)

== Local Information ==
=== Address ===
946 Taki, Katsuragi Town, Ito District, Wakayama, Japan

=== Access ===
* '''By Car:''' 20 minutes from [[Kasada Station]] (JR [[Wakayama Line]]).
* 15 minutes from [[Katsuragi Nishi Interchange]] (''Kyōnan-Wa Expressway'').

== Toyohara Family Residence ==
[[File:Toyohara House.jpg|thumb|Toyohara Family Residence]]
Located in the Taki district, the Toyohara Family Residence has been designated a [[Registered Tangible Cultural Property]] since December 5, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.town.katsuragi.wakayama.jp/20191210134032.html|title=豊原家住宅・的場家住宅・神野阿弥陀堂が登録有形文化財に登録されました！|publisher=Katsuragi Town|accessdate=2021-02-07}}</ref> The residence comprises:
* '''Main House:''' Constructed during the late [[Edo period]], renovated in 2019. A single-story wooden structure with a thatched roof and ''irimoya'' style, covering 102 square meters.
* '''Detached Sitting Room:''' Built in the early [[Shōwa era]], it features an ''irimoya'' roof, tile roofing, and measures 64 square meters.
